title: Parallelize long-prefill GDN partitions with exact state correction
decision: Current native state-passing CTAs parallelize heads/value strips while looping sequentially over NT chunks. Reached author SM120 source computes independent partition summaries and corrects initial states before its main kernel. It also uses a gate-driven approximation that can discard incoming-state influence; that shortcut is not qualified. This is a conditional long-prefill scheduling question, separate from accepted decode replay overlap.
next_step: Classify exact affine partition summaries/correction against current state passing for relevant long-prefill lengths, first including D-by-D summary storage/transfer, correction work, extra launches and actual workload frequency. Keep complete affine correction enabled as the initial numerical reference; compare the full supported prefill phase if operator evidence admits a useful route.
qualification: Preserve FP32 persistent state, native ratio3/head mapping, represented GDN formula, variable sequence boundaries and snapshots with an independent FP32/FP64 output/final-state oracle. A gate sum below -10 alone does not bound omitted-state error without incoming-state magnitudes and transition norms. Source chunk32 and state downcasts do not define native semantics. The frozen wrapper mentions unpinned0.1.2; the separately inspected author source is0.1.3, not proven installed there. Scratch capacity, graph lifetime and complete-phase benefit remain unqualified; no speedup has been measured.

title: Assess the convolution-output to recurrence boundary
decision: An actual reached foreign producer combines convolution/SiLU with grouped recurrent GDN. Native already fuses projection and convolution, Q/K normalization inside recurrence, and A/B control transforms with normalization/projection. Only convolution Q/K/V output handoff into recurrence is a separate boundary; this differs from recurrence-to-gated-RMS fusion.
next_step: Classify a closed projection/convolution-to-recurrence composition against the existing NVFP4 matrix epilogue at supported widths and batch1–6. Include ratio3 state tiles, synchronization and reuse. Reject a route that needs repeated projection or sacrifices the matrix schedule for less handoff traffic.
qualification: Evaluate the complete formula from represented projection/convolution/control inputs with an independent oracle. Preserve observable BF16 convolution history, explicit replay casts/records, FP32 persistent recurrence, snapshots, valid prefixes and lane/slot identity. Removed unobservable Q/K/V materialization can use a qualified private fused precision profile; unfused BF16 staging parity is not mandatory. Foreign producer grouping and one-kernel composition supply no native gain or admission proof.

title: Compare exponent-scaled FP16 high/low MMA with native TF32
decision: A reached register-resident window fold uses exponent-scaled FP16 high/low MMA corrections and finishes before optional Phi/anchor latch work. Native already has register-resident FP32 state and TF32 MMA; the distinct question is a separable private arithmetic/instruction schedule, without foreign LS6 rotations or latch state.
next_step: Make a cheap classifier comparison of high/low FP16 MMA affine window folding versus current TF32 at native head/value128, ratio3 and actual active widths. Include correction/packing/exponent costs and CTA geometry before any kernel implementation or performance experiment.
qualification: Use the same complete independent recurrence oracle from represented BF16 operands and FP32 initial state; check exponent extremes, overflow/subnormals and accumulated state error. Preserve FP32 persistent state, accepted-only transaction and graph/record lifetimes. Foreign W16/full-state CTA, contiguous rings and downstream Phi/Cholesky/anchor work are not native admission. No numerical or speed benefit is proved.

title: Amortize persistent GDN checkpoint writes across accepted rounds
decision: Native folds every licensed accepted prefix into FP32 state each round. Actual foreign producer retains a request-indexed committed-history ring, reconstructs outputs through triangular WY updates and folds checkpoint only on capacity/track triggers. This reduces full-state write frequency at the cost of history traffic/reconstruction, distinct from long-prefill partitioning, register residency or putting each fold on another stream.
next_step: First classify a bounded accepted-history versus state-traffic cost at native ratio3,head128,B1–6 and real accepted widths, including reconstruction work, capacity flush and tracking. Only if the bound admits a useful route, design one owner for the logical FP32 state with complete reconstruction on every supported state read and checkpoint.
qualification: Preserve native logical FP32 persistent-state semantics, accepted-only transaction, lane/request identity, convolution history, all checkpoint/track paths and stable graph lifetime. Foreign BF16 high/low persistent history, TF32 key products, WY reassociation and four-BF16-MMA fold are unqualified numerical profiles; author bit-identity prose is not evidence. Evaluate complete independent FP32/FP64 recurrence/final-state oracles over multi-round accumulation and exponent extremes before admission. Current selected worker has an actual unexpected-keyword call, so no working-engine or measured gain is claimed. Imported host suffix corpus remains unqualified and is not part of this state question.

title: Classify dependent launch on the recurrence-to-gatednorm edge
decision: Native already owns the dependent-launch facility and a prior A8 weight-prefetch trial regressed and was not kept. Actual foreign recurrent producer waits before global loads then releases dependent launch immediately; its gatednorm waits before all input loads and releases after output stores on the small-width path. The specific recurrence-to-gatednorm edge is untried here, with very little independent setup to hide. This is distinct from cross-stream accepted-state fold overlap and from producer/norm fusion.
next_step: Use a cheap classifier to bound genuinely independent consumer work before the required wait, CTA resources and producer/consumer contention. Reject if setup is negligible or contention predicts regression. Only an admitted distinct edge merits native graph/oracle qualification; do not repeat the rejected A8 prefetch trial.
qualification: Launch release does not establish output readiness; every consumer path must synchronize before dependent global loads, and every producer CTA must release or exit according to the existing API. Preserve native FP32 persistent state, valid record/snapshot/publication and capture lifetime. Source scheduling and capability names are not hardware, race, numerical or performance qualification. No native PDL facility gap or measured benefit is asserted.
